extracted.intended_audience: researchers conducting systematic reviews and methodological studies on dissemination/publication bias in health and related research
extracted.subtask_description: Protocol and methodological guidance for a systematic review to identify, categorise, and critically appraise empirical and methodological studies about dissemination (publication-related) bias in health research, and to assess methods to prevent/detect/mitigate such biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — empirical studies (inclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical studies are defined as those that provide empirical evidence on the existence, consequences, causes and/or risk factors of dissemination bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include studies that provide empirical evidence on existence, consequences, causes and/or risk factors of types of dissemination bias; these will be identified from searches and assessed for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — methodological studies (inclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological studies are defined as those that have developed or investigated methods for preventing, reducing or detecting dissemination bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include studies that develop or evaluate methods for preventing, reducing or detecting dissemination bias; these will be categorised and appraised for assumptions, usefulness, limitations and required resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of review (domain restriction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on dissemination bias in health and related research (medical and health related research); social sciences yielded few studies in preliminary searches so focus is limited to health-related fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review will concentrate on health and related research; however references and citation searching may identify earlier or cross-disciplinary studies to include where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature search — core databases and complementary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Search the Cochrane Methodology Register (CRM) and MEDLINE (since 1998) and compare results; additionally search EMBASE (selected years), Ahmed, CINAHL, PsychInfo, SIGLE, Dissertation Abstracts, reference lists and citation searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MEDLINE and CRM compared to check completeness/usefulness; EMBASE/Ahmed/Cinahl/PsychInfo/SIGLE/Dissertation Abstracts searched (1998-2007 ranges specified) with some searches conducted by one reviewer; no language restriction; use references and citation searches to supplement database searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search term checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Key words to be used include: publication bias, dissemination bias, language bias, national bias, country bias, reporting bias, grey literature bias, conference/abstract bias, full publication bias, citation bias, time lag/delay bias, reference bias, selection bias, location bias, duplication or multiple publication bias, database bias, index bias, file drawer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed keywords when searching electronic databases and in iterative search strategies; include titles with or without abstracts for initial screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening and selection — dual review
rubrics_metrics.description: References (titles with or without abstracts) gathered by searching the CMR and MEDLINE will be assessed independently by two reviewers for inclusion or exclusion; any disagreement will be discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where specified, use independent dual screening to reduce selection bias; note that some database searches (EMBASE, Ahmed, CINAHL, PsychInfo, SIGLE, Dissertation Abstracts) will be conducted by one reviewer with checking procedures described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of identified studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify identified studies as (1) evidence studies or (2) methodological studies; some studies may be classified as both an evidence and a methods study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a pre-specified structure (framework of dissemination profile) to facilitate assessment and synthesis; use standardised classification forms (Appendix 1/2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence studies — dissemination profile categorisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence studies will be categorised into various types of dissemination bias according to a framework of dissemination profile: non-publication (never, or delayed); incomplete publication (e.g. biased outcome reporting, data-dredged subgroup effects, biased full publication of conference abstracts); published but difficult to access (e.g. grey literature, language bias, database bias); other biased dissemination activities (e.g. citation bias, duplicate bias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some studies may belong to more than one category; categorise consistently using the framework to enable synthesis across types of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence studies — direct vs indirect evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate evidence studies into direct evidence and indirect evidence. Direct evidence refers to data or observations that could be used to directly indicate dissemination bias (e.g. admissions of bias, comparison of published vs unpublished study results, prospective/retrospective follow-up of cohorts of studies). Indirect evidence refers to observations that could be explained indirectly by dissemination bias (e.g. disproportionately high proportion of positive findings in published literature; larger effect sizes in smaller studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this distinction when assessing the strength of evidence; direct evidence will be prioritised for critical appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assessment checklist for direct empirical studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a checklist to critically appraise studies that provided direct empirical evidence (and studies assessing association between sample size and effects in multiple meta-analyses) with regard to scientific rigorousness, the sample’s representativeness, and appropriateness of data analyses and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific checklist items include: scientific rigorousness (e.g. prospective studies more valid than retrospective; selection/inclusion biases; independent duplication of assessments), generalisability (applicability to different fields/settings/designs), appropriateness of data analysis (methods suited to objectives), and appropriateness of interpretation (limitations considered). Topic-specific items may be added as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardised appraisal forms and independent assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a standardised appraisal form (Appendix 1), categorisation of all evidence studies and critical appraisal of selected studies will be independently carried out by two reviewers; disagreements will be resolved by discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure independent duplicate appraisal for key studies to reduce bias; document disagreements and resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological studies — classification and cross-classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Method studies will be categorised according to methods they investigated and then cross-classified by (1) type of dissemination bias and (2) stage of literature review (pre-, during-, post-review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a standardised method classification sheet (Appendix 2); one reviewer conducts review with checking by a second reviewer; disagreements resolved by discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical appraisal of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Available methods will be critically appraised in terms of underlying assumptions, conditions in which to be used, usefulness, limitations, and resource required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess each method’s assumptions and applicability; provide practical commentary on usefulness and resource implications for reviewers and policy makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and synthesis of findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Data extracted from the included studies and results of critical appraisal will be presented in tables and described narratively; if appropriate, results from individual studies will be quantitatively pooled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider pooling (e.g. pooled odds ratio of full publication of conference abstracts with statistically significant vs non-significant results) where appropriate; take critical appraisal into account when interpreting pooled results; highlight contradictions or strengthening of previous evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of dissemination bias within empirical evidence studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorise results of included empirical evidence studies as positive (significant dissemination bias), non-significant (no clear dissemination bias), or 'can't tell'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Then examine the association of study results with study quality and dissemination profile (including time of publication, journal impact factor, number of citations after a given period, and study's impact on guidelines/recommendations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to sampling published systematic reviews for assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a representative sample of published systematic reviews (both narrative and quantitative/meta-analytic) that evaluated healthcare interventions, diagnostic test accuracy, and epidemiological association studies to examine measures taken to prevent, reduce and detect dissemination bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address shortcomings of previous assessments (e.g. DARE-restricted sample) by ensuring representativeness across review types and topics; assess methods used within those reviews for dealing with publication/dissemination bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative assessment of bibliographic sources for methodological reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare studies identified from MEDLINE with those from the Cochrane Methodology Register to check the completeness and usefulness of the two bibliographic databases for methodological reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the comparison to inform search strategy completeness and guide supplementary searching (references, citation searches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and role of funnel plot and related statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Funnel plot and related statistical methods have been applied to collections of meta-analyses to estimate possible publication bias; previous conclusion was that available statistical methods for detecting and adjusting publication bias should be mainly used for sensitivity analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appraising or applying funnel-plot based/statisical methods, consider their assumptions, power, and role as sensitivity analyses rather than definitive adjustments; critically appraise these methods in methodological study review.
